question: Doubling carbon dioxide from 280 to 560 ppm adds about 3.7 watts per square metre. How many more does doubling again to 1,120 ppm add?
answer: About 3.7 watts per square metre more.
move: When effects follow ratios, each doubling counts the same, not each unit.
ask: Where do I expect twice the effort to give twice the result, when returns actually shrink?
trap: Twice as much gas seems to need twice the push, so 7.4.
hint: The push depends on the ratio of new to old concentration.
steps: The push grows with the logarithm of the ratio: 5.35 × ln(C ÷ C₀)
560 to 1,120 ppm is again a ratio of 2: 5.35 × ln 2 ≈ 3.7
About 3.7 watts per square metre more.

notes.text: Close to the level of the mid-2020s: 2.2 watts per square metre.
The first doubling: 3.7 watts per square metre.
Doubling again adds the same 3.7, not twice as much.

source: Myhre et al., Geophysical Research Letters, 1998
reference: Myhre, Highwood, Shine & Stordal, New estimates of radiative forcing due to well mixed greenhouse gases, Geophysical Research Letters, 1998
